question.problem:
Find the solutions of $20x≡8\,(\text{mod}\,28).$ Express your answers as nonnegative integers smaller than $28,$ and in ascending order. 

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*

question.worked_solution:
In the given congruence, we have $a=20$ and $n=28$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(20,28)=4.
$$

Since $b=8$ is divisible by $4,$ our congruence has $4$ solutions.

First, we use the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}20x & ≡8 &  & (\text{mod}\,28) \\ 4\cdot 5x & ≡4\cdot 2 &  & (\text{mod}\,4\cdot 7) \\ \cancel{4}\cdot 5x & ≡\cancel{4}\cdot 2 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{4}\cdot 7) \\ 5x & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in the new congruence, we have ${a}_{1}=5$ and ${n}_{1}=7$, where

$$
\text{gcd}({a}_{1},{n}_{1})=\text{gcd}(5,7)=1.
$$

So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo $7.$

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,7).$ To find the inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,7),$ we compute the exponents of $5\,(\text{mod}\,7)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,7):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2} & ≡25≡3\cdot 7+4≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ {5}^{3} & ≡4\cdot 5≡20≡2\cdot 7+6≡6 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ {5}^{4} & ≡6\cdot 5≡30≡4\cdot 7+2≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ {5}^{5} & ≡2\cdot 5≡10≡1\cdot 7+3≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ {5}^{6} & ≡3\cdot 5≡15≡2\cdot 7+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $3\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,7),$ which means that $3$ is the multiplicative inverse of $5$ (modulo $7$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $3,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ 3\cdot 5x & ≡3\cdot 2 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ (3\cdot 5)x & ≡6 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ x & ≡6 &  & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the solution $x≡6\,(\text{mod}\,7).$ 

But our original congruence was modulo $28$ (not modulo $7$). To find all the solutions modulo $28,$ we repeatedly add $7$ modulo $28$ until we reach the number $6$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡6 &  & (\text{mod}\,28) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡6+7≡13 &  & (\text{mod}\,28) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡13+7≡20 &  & (\text{mod}\,28) \\ {x}_{4} & ≡20+7≡27 &  & (\text{mod}\,28) \\ {x}_{5} & ≡27+7≡34≡28+6≡6≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,28)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are 

$$
{x}_{1,2,3,4}≡6,\,13,\,20,\,27\,(\text{mod}\,28).
$$
